rowNumberingFinding.statement: In the CAD and in the guide-data per-pin envelopes, pin 1 sits 2.23 mm from the PCB header edge and pin 2 4.77 mm from it, so the odd row runs along the board edge. A real Pi has the even row along the edge (pin 1 on the inner row); guide/content/steps.py already says so in step gpio. All per-pin results here use the real (physical) rows.

addedMaterialSampled0.25mm.note: sampled; the exact minimum along the descent is at most 0.125 mm lower

csi.note: straight distance from the camera connector to the Pi CSI connector (routes.json head_csi end points); ribbon 200 mm

C_sideEffects.note: The PCB sits on the rails, so its gap to the cap is zero by design; component gaps are in A_finalPose.

descent-rails.json.method:
Cap-on descent clearance of the added rail material only (pieces of C - C_V1.6 with volume >= 0.001 mm3), for the
released V1.7 cap and the candidate, one cap at a time. The boolean difference also leaves zero-volume surface slivers
on the unchanged shell (re-exported vertices differ in the last digits); those are counted and excluded here.
Sampled every 0.25 mm over h = 0..40; gap is 1-Lipschitz in a translation, so the true minimum is at most 0.125 mm below
the sampled one.  Usage: descent_rails.py <candidate-world.stl>.  Writes ../descent-rails.json.

static-pi.json.method:
Static spacing between the Pi (carried by the cap rails) and the cap itself, for the printed V1.6, the released V1.7
and the candidate, so inherited spacings can be told apart from new ones. Each Pi part is moved with its seat
([0,0,0], [-4.6,0,0], [-DX,0,DZ]) and measured against the whole cap, the rail zone (|y| >= 25.3) and the rest.
These parts never move relative to the cap, so the 2 mm descent criterion does not apply; the numbers are stack-ups.
Usage: DX=3.3 DZ=2.0 static_pi.py <candidate-world.stl>.  Writes ../static-pi.json.
